tasks.title: Lessons spliced by recurring class
tasks.summary: lessonsForDispatch splices recurring and epic-repeating classes (other.unclassified included), withholds the rest with a read command.
tasks.objective: Implement epic-spec D2 with the operator's thresholds (decision 14): new module src/lessonRecurrence.ts (`errorClassCounts(events, {now, windowDays})`, one named constant each for RECUR_MIN_TASKS=3, RECUR_WINDOW_DAYS=30, EPIC_REPEAT_MIN=1) and the selection rules in `lessonsForDispatch`: agent-role and claim-path untouched; every stack-wide/case-type/security lesson is spliced only when its class recurs store-wide or repeats in the dispatch's epic, otherwise withheld; `other.unclassified` follows the same rule as every class (decision 13); a lesson with no `error_class`, or with a class no longer in taxonomy.yml, is read as `other.unclassified` and the result carries a warning naming the lesson id and the stale value; nothing is withheld from a security-reviewer. Add options `{events, epicId, now, full, class}`. Event identity (D2; the event envelope has no `epic_id`, event.schema.json is `additionalProperties: false`): class = `payload.error`; task = `eventTaskId(record) ?? payload.task_ref` (events.ts `eventTaskId`, the rule agents-registry.ts's `error-logged` fold already uses: reuse it, do not re-implement it), and distinct-task counting uses that identity, so repeated events on one task count once; epic = `payload.epic_id ?? epicOfTaskId(task)` (taskId.ts), `payload.epic_id` winning when both exist; an event with a task but no epic counts store-wide only, never toward an epic; an event with no task identity is skipped; with no `epicId` nothing counts as an epic repeat; return `withheld` and `warnings`, and omit the `lessons` array unless `full`; append one trailing line naming each withheld class, its count and `bs lessons for-dispatch --class <group.class>`. New src/lessonEvents.ts `readRecurrenceEvents(stateDir, {now, windowDays})`, the one store reader the CLI and brief compose use: every session id from `listSessionIds(stateDir)` (events.ts), skipping a session file whose mtime is older than `now - windowDays` (safe by the invariant epic-spec D2 states: events.ts `appendEventLocked` stamps every `ts` at write time and `keptTs` is `prompts-`-only and refuses a future `ts`, so a file's mtime is never earlier than its newest event's `ts`, up to the file system's timestamp granularity), each read with `readEvents` (events.ts); cost bound: one `stat` per session file and one `readEvents` per in-window file, never one for an older file (`stat` and `readEvents` injectable so the test can count them), keeping `error-logged` events whose timestamp lies in the window; a missing dir returns []. Failing tests first: factory/orchestrator/test/lessonRecurrence.test.ts, factory/orchestrator/test/lessonsByClass.test.ts and factory/orchestrator/test/lessonEvents.test.ts. TDD: write the named failing test first, watch it fail, implement minimally, watch it pass. Read factory/specs/active/bs-optimize/epic-spec.md before starting.
acceptance_criteria: Epic criterion 3: every selection case in criterion 3 has a fixture test (3 error-logged on distinct tasks in 30 days spliced; 2 withheld and named; an event older than 30 days not counted; epic repeat of 1 spliced; `other.unclassified` withheld without recurrence and spliced on repeat; a class-less or stale-class lesson read as `other.unclassified` with a warning; agent-role/claim-path never withheld; security-reviewer withholds nothing).
Epic criterion 4 (module half): without `full` the result has no `lessons` array; `class` returns exactly that class's approved lessons.

Store-wide means every session (S2-7): lessonEvents.test.ts builds a temporary state dir with two session files; a class logged on 2 tasks in session A and 1 task in session B within 30 days recurs; a session file whose mtime is older than 30 days is not opened (injected `readEvents` spy); an event inside a recent file but older than 30 days is dropped; a missing state dir returns []. lessonEvents.test.ts also asserts the cost bound: `stat` is called once per session file and `readEvents` exactly once per in-window file. lessonEvents.test.ts also pins the invariant the mtime skip rests on (epic-spec D2): an event appended through `appendEvent` (events.ts) with `stateDir` a temporary dir has a `ts` no later than its session file's mtime (`Date.parse(ts) <= mtimeMs + 2000`, the 2,000 ms covering file-system timestamp granularity: Linux's coarse kernel clock, 1 s on HFS+), so a future change that stamps `ts` ahead of the write fails it. lessonsByClass.test.ts shows an event of epic E counts as a repeat for `epicId: E` and not for another epic, and that no `epicId` means no repeat.

Event identity (S2-major round 4), one test each in lessonsByClass.test.ts, every fixture an envelope event.schema.json accepts (no envelope `epic_id`): (a) an `error-logged` event carrying only the envelope `task_id` (no `payload.task_ref`) is counted, under that task id's epic; (b) three `error-logged` events of one class on the same task are one task, not a recurrence; (c) `payload.epic_id` wins over the task id's epic when both exist; (d) an event with no task identity (no envelope or payload `task_id`, no `payload.task_ref`) is skipped and counts toward no class; an event with an unqualified task id and no `payload.epic_id` counts store-wide and toward no epic.

tasks.title: bs cleanup module
tasks.summary: Finds merged task worktrees, their branches and orphan dirs, and removes only what is provably idle and merged.
tasks.objective: Implement epic-spec D10 module half (decision 16a): new module src/cleanup.ts exporting `planCleanup(opts)` -> `{items: [{kind, path?, branch?, action, reason}], warnings}` and `runCleanup(opts)` (dry run by default; with `apply: true` it calls planCleanup itself in the same run and then acts, so no removal list is ever read from a file or an earlier run). Options: `projectDir`, `epicId?`, `apply`, `now`, `events` (store events; an `epic-closed` event closes an epic, read via `readClosedEpicWidths` in src/epicWidth.ts), and injectable deps (`git`, `stat`/`readdir`, `isPidAlive` defaulting to T8's `pidIsAlive` from src/heavyLock.ts, where only `ESRCH` means dead and `EPERM` or any other error means alive, `trash`, `platform`, `heavyLockDir`). Targets: (1) registered worktrees on `bs/<epic>/<task>` (or legacy `smith/`) branches whose branch is an ancestor of the epic's integration branch or the default branch, with that branch; (2) directories under `<parent>/.wt/<basename>/` that git does not register; (3) `git worktree prune`. Safety rules, each its own test: skip anything active in the last 24 h (newest of the branch's last commit time, the worktree index mtime, the newest file mtime found walking the tree without following symlinks, stopping at the first entry newer than 24 h and at 20,000 entries, which keeps the item as `walk-capped`; an EACCES or ENOENT during the walk keeps the item as `unreadable` with the path); skip every task of an open epic, and never remove an integration branch or its worktree unless that branch is an ancestor of the default branch; skip dirty worktrees and report them; skip any name containing `harness-codex-dispatch`; respect locks (the T8 heavy lock via `readHeavyLock` when its cwd is inside the item, git `index.lock`, a worktree marked `locked`) unless the lock records a pid that is dead; when unsure, keep the item and report why; immediately before each branch deletion and each worktree removal, re-run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> <target>` for the item's merge target (the epic's integration branch, local `<default>` or `origin/<default>`: merged into any one of them counts, since each is landed history) and keep the item (`not-merged`) when it fails: this gate, not `git branch -d`, is the safety, because `-d` only checks against the current HEAD or upstream; then remove only with `git worktree remove` (no `--force`) and `git branch -d` (never `-D`), and report a `-d` refusal as `keep` with git's message; the order per worktree item is gate, `git worktree remove`, gate again, `git branch -d` (an uncommitted edit made after the gate makes the removal refuse, a commit made after the first gate fails the second); a failed removal, a failed second gate or a failed deletion is reported `keep` with the reason or git's message, never retried or forced, and the branch is then not deleted; move unregistered directories to the Trash with `/usr/bin/trash` on macOS and on any other platform report them `manual` and remove nothing; never `rm -rf`, never touch a path outside `<parent>/.wt/<basename>/` (the candidate's realpath against the root's realpath, so a symlinked root is resolved first; an entry under the root that is a symlink is kept as `symlink`, never followed, trashed or removed) or a branch outside the project's `bs/` / `smith/` prefixes; never kill a process; never fetch (merge checks read local `<default>` and `origin/<default>` refs). Reuse src/worktree.ts: export `detectDefaultBranch`, export `parseWorktreePorcelain` extended to read `locked`, `detached` and `prunable` (each a bare line or the keyword plus a reason; a `locked` worktree is always kept, its free-text reason never read for a pid; a `prunable` entry is left to `git worktree prune`, never passed to `git worktree remove`), and keep `removeTaskWorktree` working for its existing callers.
